issue_context.title: Extract spider switch energy attributes into sensors
issue_context.body:
This issue is for the switch platform of the spider integration.

The switch integration has embedded sensors for energy usage. This is no longer the preferred approach. Integrations using this approach should turn this data into standalone sensors.

This is important because Home Assistant is going to introduce home energy management (HEM) in 2021.8. HEM will be able to consume the data if it is exposed as standalone sensors.

To make sure that the sensors that represent total kWh is usable for HEM, set `state_class` to `measurement` and set `last_reset` to the timestamp of when the meter got reset (midnight if daily etc). [See sensor documentation for more information.](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor)

[Link to the architecture discussion.](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/579)

review_comments:
These entities, together with the switch entities, are now all polling the same plug individually. Would that cause problems? As it triples the number of requests (that are likely to happen at exactly the same time).

Better would be to implement a DataUpdateCoordinator, that fetched the data once and next notifies all entities.

Good question. I don't believe so as the library only polls on certain refresh rates; https://github.com/peternijssen/spiderpy/blob/1.4.2/spiderpy/spiderapi.py#L55

I've read about the DataUpdateCoordinator. Perhaps I can update the component in a separate MR with strict typing, DataUpdateCoordinator, etc.

Unless you believe otherwise of course. Then I'll update it within this MR :)
Doing that in a separate PR is absolutely fine. I was just reaching out to confirm it is not causing problems at this point. Thanks! 👍
It would be nice to type the parameters here since most other things are typed.

I've also added STATE_CLASS_MEASUREMENT, assuming this is a current measurement that is displayed here.

```suggestion
class SpiderPowerPlugPower(SensorEntity):
    """Representation of a Spider Power Plug (power)."""

    _attr_device_class = DEVICE_CLASS_POWER
    _attr_state_class = STATE_CLASS_MEASUREMENT
    _attr_unit_of_measurement = POWER_WATT
```
We reserve the word entity for `Entity` instances. Please rename the variable to eg `plug`.

```suggestion
class SpiderPowerPlugEnergy(SensorEntity):
    """Representation of a Spider Power Plug (energy)."""

    _attr_unit_of_measurement = ENERGY_KILO_WATT_HOUR
    _attr_device_class = DEVICE_CLASS_ENERGY
    _attr_state_class = STATE_CLASS_MEASUREMENT

```
